name: claude-dashboard
description: "Use this for a local, data-backed dashboard, metrics page, KPI tracker, scorecard, data visualization or recurring report that opens in the bundled live editor: a page or scroll story of charts, numbers and tables over datasets (a CSV/TSV/JSON file the user has, or data you gather and attach), with a Sources panel that shows where every number comes from. Read it when creating, filling, refreshing or revising one. You write the datasets, then the page as plain HTML, into the dashboard's own store with this skill's script. Not for a static HTML mockup or a picture of a dashboard."

name: claude-data
description: "Use this for a local, data-backed dashboard, metrics page, KPI tracker, scorecard, data visualization or recurring report that opens in the bundled live editor: a page or scroll story of charts, numbers and tables over datasets (a CSV/TSV/JSON or text file the user has, or data you gather and attach), with a Sources panel that shows where every number comes from. Read it when creating, filling, refreshing or revising one. You write the datasets, then the page as plain HTML, into the dashboard's own store with this skill's script. Not for a static HTML mockup or a picture of a dashboard."

name: claude-motion
description: "Use this for a local Motion film: a short animated video (10–30 s unless asked for more, 900 s at most), such as an explainer, product walkthrough or UI demo, launch teaser, logo sting, social clip, animated chart or title sequence, that plays in the bundled Motion player and exports from there to MP4 or GIF. A narrated one carries a voice track: a take a scene, made here with a speech provider of the user's or recorded by them, spoken and captioned by the player, the motion timed to its words. Everything on screen is code, a pure function of time, written scene by scene into the film's own store with this skill's script while the user watches it fill in. Read it when creating, continuing, finalizing or revising one. Not for editing real footage, subtitles or audio (that is a video editor), a still picture, a slide deck or a static HTML page."

name: claude-whiteboard
description: "Use this for a local Whiteboard: a shared space for laying out thinking in whatever form it needs (a diagram, a flow, a map of ideas, a plan, a comparison, a drawn explanation, a small working embed) that opens in the bundled board editor, where people move, draw, comment and send comments to the agent. Its content lives in the board's own store, written with this skill's script, never in files you edit by hand. Read it before you create a board or change one. Not for a slide deck, a document, a film or a static HTML page."

name: dataviz
description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium (HTML/React artifact, inline SVG, matplotlib/plotly/d3/Recharts, PNG). Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method - form heuristic, color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, interaction rules. Default palette in references/palette.md.

name: motion-director
description: "Use this to make a finished motion video that has something to say: an explainer, a product or feature video, a data story, an article or report retold, a social short, an opener or title sting, or any other film with a point, most often with a voice-over. It works as the film's director: finds the one point and the picture that carries it, writes the narration for the ear, has it voiced with a speech provider the user picks, times every scene to the words, builds the film with the claude-motion skill, looks at its frames the way a viewer would and hands over the film in its player, open beside the chat from the first minute, to watch, comment on and change, with a film folder that stays editable; the MP4 follows when the user asks for it. Needs claude-motion installed beside it. Not for a quick animation with no script (claude-motion alone), editing real footage, or AI-generated video clips."

name: release-skills
description: Universal release workflow. Auto-detects version files and changelogs. Supports Node.js, Python, Rust, Claude Plugin, GitHub Releases, annotated tags, historical release backfill, and generic projects. Use when user says "release", "发布", "new version", "bump version", "push", "推送", "release notes", "GitHub Release", or "回填 Release".
